content:
Hi everyone,

My name is Ronan Terpereau, and I am a researcher in algebraic geometry at the University of Lille. Together with Lionel Rieg, a colleague computer scientist at the Verimag laboratory, we are working on formalizing the classification of flag varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero in Lean, using OpenAI’s GPT Sol to write most of the proofs.

Our approach is to:

  1. Prove the classification of standard parabolic subgroups for groups equipped with a BN-pair.
  2. Construct a BN-pair for connected reductive algebraic groups, and establish the appropriate uniqueness statement.

The classification is still work in progress. Along the way, we have obtained a formalization of the Lie-Kolchin theorem, which we have separated from the main project. (Lie-Kolchin theorem proves that a connected solvable subgroup of GLn over an algebraically closed field can be conjugated into the upper triangular subgroup.) It is quite short: less than 2.000 lines in total. 

We are now going back through this part by hand, reviewing and reorganizing the proofs with a possible mathlib contribution in mind. 

  • Would this be a reasonable candidate for mathlib? In particular, is there anything we should keep in mind given the substantial use of AI in developing the proofs? We would also appreciate advice on how to fit the statements and supporting definitions into existing mathlib infrastructure before preparing a PR.
  • For the broader classification project, would a separate repository depending on mathlib be the most natural home, or is there an existing project we should coordinate with?

We would be happy to hear from anyone interested in this, especially people working on algebraic groups.

Ronan

Using AI is not recommended for new contributors to mathlib. Other maintainers may have different views, but I think that it is important to learn how to write good Lean code by hand. For this particular subject, I believe that some coordination should occur in order to find the better approach towards the study of reductive groups (over arbitrary fields) and in connection with the current effort towards the formalization of the classification of simple complex Lie algebras.

Hey Ronan! Good to see you here. Do you already have some code that you are ready to share?
And are you aware of the Tau Ceti project? It builds on top of Mathlib, and is a place where the community builds a high quality formal library using AI. Happy to discuss this more!
